author: reek
body: An imperfect-information model of what an agent knows about its opponent's cards. Magic is a hidden-information game: you do not see the opponent's hand, but you do see cards they reveal, discard, cast, or that get exiled. A good agent remembers those and tracks where each seen card is now -- still in hand, on the battlefield, in the graveyard, or exiled -- so it can play around a known counterspell, or press when it knows the opponent is empty-handed.

author: reek
body: This module is pure belief bookkeeping: observations move a known card between locations; queries ask where a card is or how many are still in hand. It reads nothing hidden -- the caller feeds it only what the agent legitimately saw.

author: reek
body: Where a seen card is believed to be. LocHand means the agent saw the card (a reveal, or inferred it was drawn) and has no later observation moving it, so it believes the opponent still holds it. Every other location is a place a card became visible: cast onto the stack, resolved to the battlefield, put in the graveyard (discard, death, spell resolution), or exiled.

author: reek
body: An agent's belief about one opponent: the set of cards it has seen, each with its last observed location. A card the agent has never seen is simply absent (its location is LocUnknown).

author: reek
body: Each observation is a thing the agent legitimately saw happen to a card, and records the card's new location. A revealed card enters the model in the opponent's hand; a cast card moves to the stack; a resolved permanent lands on the battlefield while a resolved spell goes to the graveyard; a discarded or destroyed card is in the graveyard; an exiled card is in exile. Casting, discarding, and exiling a card the agent had believed in hand all correctly stop counting it as held.
